_comment: Conformance spec for the meshbench dataset. This file is the DECLARED
expectation the battery gates on; bench/GROUND-TRUTH-clickhouse.json is the
source-captured expectation it gates aggregates against. They are two
independently maintained records and the battery cross-checks them where
they overlap (RF-002 null counts), so a stale file is itself a finding
Derived, not guessed: the column types below were read off a real
clickhouse -> ArrowIpcSink artifact of meshbench.perf_1m pulled on the
ground-truth-era pipeline, and they match the field-for-field schema pinned
string_width_tolerant applies the B-3 cross-lane fence: `string` and
`large_string` are both valid Arrow strings, meshroad reads both, and which
one appears is a property of the LANE (pandas 3.0's string dtype yields
large_string; DuckDB's native Arrow export yields plain utf8), not of
_discriminators_comment: RF-002. The floor is one DECLARED discriminator, not a generic count of
nullable columns: a bare '>= N nullable columns' rule is vacuous on a wide
dataset and unsatisfiable on a narrow one. meshbench has exactly one
nullable column, so the gate here is that `score` discriminates with an
EXACT null count, cross-checked against the ground-truth file's own
_boundary_comment: B-2 / transfer doctrine. Aggregate parity is blind to a uniform shift: move
every timestamp by eight hours and count, sum, null count and cardinality
all still match. min/max is the cheapest check that is NOT invariant under
that shift, which is exactly why it is mandatory.

aggregates._note: AUTHORITY. Order-independent integer arithmetic; this one gates.
Corroborates only. round(sum(float)) is order-sensitive because the source sums float64 in parallel and float addition is not associative.

_serve_gate_comment: The workload the zero-copy gate runs, twice, against the artifact. It must
touch at least one column so the cold pass actually decodes something; it
deliberately does NOT touch all 14, because projection pushdown skipping
the untouched ones is correct behaviour and the counters should show it.
serve_gate_sql: SELECT status, sum(amount), count(*) FROM {table} GROUP BY status
